title: Split-allocator residency profiles and trace-guided KV prefetch for ultra-long contexts (Llama/Mistral/Qwen)
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: produce per-model, per-variant GPU memory profiles and a split-allocator policy that reduces OOMs and memory tail variance for 16k+ contexts while preserving p99 latency and batching throughput. This ticket covers design, experiments, and a staged rollout for Llama-2 family variants, Mistral large-context configs, and Qwen-extended models.

Context: Existing memory profiles are insufficient for heterogeneous quantized shards and persistent KV residency when continuous batching mixes short and ultra-long requests. We see OOMs and opportunistic eviction that causes latency spikes and correctness risks.

Deliverables:
- New split-allocator strategy that separates KV-resident pools vs ephemeral activation allocations with explicit per-variant residency hints.
- A trace-guided prefetch/eviction heuristic tuned per model-variant and context length distribution.
- Memory profile artifacts (CSV + human-readable) for Llama-2-70B-chat, Mistral-7B-long, Qwen-14B-32k variants for seq_len = [8192,16384,32768].
- Benchmarks showing OOM reduction, throughput and latency delta, and token-cost implications.
- Rollout plan for hosted and Dedicated with canary config and automatic fallback to conservative profiles.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Reduce OOM incidents on 16k+ runsets by >=95% in internal stress tests. 2) p99 latency change <= +5% for mixed workloads (50% short <512, 50% long >=8k) at target throughput. 3) No correctness regressions (identical outputs) when fallback not triggered. 4) Profiles stored in /profiles/memory/v2 and surfaced in console release runtime-1.20.

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: aggressive prefetching can push ephemeral allocations into GPU OOMs under short-heavy workloads. Mitigation: adaptive budget throttling based on recent allocation pressure and continuous-batching backlog. Risk: model-specific heuristics may not generalize across quantization formats. Mitigation: automated profile selection with fallback to conservative profile and alerting when telemetry divergence > 20%.
experiments_plan: Matrix: models = [llama-2-13b, llama-2-70b-chat, mistral-7b-long, qwen-14b-32k]; seq_lens = [8192,16384,32768]; quant = [fp16, int8-q4_k_m, awq4]; batch_mix = [100% long, 50/50 short-long, 90% short]. Metrics: OOM count, p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput (tokens/s), allocator fragmentation, KV-eviction rate, token-cost delta. Use dedicated infra with deterministic seeds and 10-run averages.
benchmarks_so_far: Initial runs (2025-02-20): Llama-2-70B-chat at 16k with conservative profile: 3 OOMs / 1000 requests; with split-allocator prototype + per-layer residency hints: 0 OOMs / 1000 requests, p99 +3.8% latency. Mistral-7B-long at 32k: fragmentation reduced by ~28% measured via slab histogram. Qwen-14B-32k shows a 12% improvement in peak memory headroom with AWQ profile. Full results: https://docs.internal.redwood/profiles/ENG-53109/initial-results (internal)
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Deploy to 5% of hosted traffic for model-variants with telemetry enabled; monitor OOMs, p99, and KV-eviction rate for 72h. Phase 2 (staged): Expand to Dedicated customers on a per-account opt-in for one week. Phase 3 (default): Flip on for mixed workloads with automatic conservative fallback if divergence triggers. Provide migration doc and CLI to pin older profiles.
monitoring_and_alerting: Add alert: memory-profile-divergence when actual GPU allocated > profile_budget + 15% for >30s. Dashboard panels: per-model resident_bytes, eviction_count, allocate_rate, fragmentation_index. SLOs: OOM rate < 0.1% per 24h per model-variant.
